case.scope: Bounded Skydio X10 reconstruction from Skydio datasheets and support pages, one supplier press release (Nidec), news reports of the October 2024 Chinese sanctions, and a U.S. customs ocean bill-of-lading snapshot (ImportYeti API, 2026-11-09). Structure: the product plus 18 items named in Skydio or supplier sources (one airframe item inferred); four image-sensor items and their makers come from a retailer listing (secondary). Suppliers: item-level associations only where a named source states them (NVIDIA, Qualcomm, Teledyne FLIR, Nidec, Sony and Samsung (retailer listing), Dongguan Poweramp (historical), Skydio final assembly); category-level associations for organisations that shipped goods to Skydio by sea on or after 2023-11-01 (X10 US shipping start), grouped by the goods in the customs descriptions. Customs records show goods shipped to Skydio, not which Skydio product they were for. Not a complete or certified production BOM; quantities only where a source states them; air freight and distributor purchases are not visible. Item-to-category classifications are researcher-derived and pending review. Every statement carries a status in the assertion audit. v0.2 adds 50 shipments (ocean bills arriving May to October 2026) and 12 port-to-port routes from bill-of-lading lookups; 36 shipments are allocated to an item through the supplier's customs-based category (researcher-derived), the rest (packaging, power supplies) to no item. Item-level supply links added for the sensor package and Connect SL radio (Skydio) and the 5G modem (Telit Cinterion). Item-level links with no customs record carry 15 modelled flows (observationStatus 'modelled', researcher-derived) from inferred or supplier-stated countries of manufacture; each origin site's evidence note gives the basis and confidence, and the Connect SL radio flow has no origin (not established).

assertion_audit.subject: <https://example.org/supply-chain-resilience/case/skydio-x10/v0.2/bom>
assertion_audit.object: "Bounded Skydio X10 reconstruction from Skydio datasheets and support pages, one supplier press release (Nidec), news reports of the October 2024 Chinese sanctions, and a U.S. customs ocean bill-of-lading snapshot (ImportYeti API, 2026-11-09). Structure: the product plus 18 items named in Skydio or supplier sources (one airframe item inferred); four image-sensor items and their makers come from a retailer listing (secondary). Suppliers: item-level associations only where a named source states them (NVIDIA, Qualcomm, Teledyne FLIR, Nidec, Sony and Samsung (retailer listing), Dongguan Poweramp (historical), Skydio final assembly); category-level associations for organisations that shipped goods to Skydio by sea on or after 2023-11-01 (X10 US shipping start), grouped by the goods in the customs descriptions. Customs records show goods shipped to Skydio, not which Skydio product they were for. Not a complete or certified production BOM; quantities only where a source states them; air freight and distributor purchases are not visible. Item-to-category classifications are researcher-derived and pending review. Every statement carries a status in the assertion audit. v0.2 adds 50 shipments (ocean bills arriving May to October 2026) and 12 port-to-port routes from bill-of-lading lookups; 36 shipments are allocated to an item through the supplier's customs-based category (researcher-derived), the rest (packaging, power supplies) to no item. Item-level supply links added for the sensor package and Connect SL radio (Skydio) and the 5G modem (Telit Cinterion). Item-level links with no customs record carry 15 modelled flows (observationStatus 'modelled', researcher-derived) from inferred or supplier-stated countries of manufacture; each origin site's evidence note gives the basis and confidence, and the Connect SL radio flow has no origin (not established)."^^<http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string>
